rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After dropping bāʾ from the negated construction, the noun may be raised; Basrans and Kufans report that usage.
rows.anchor: ما فيك براغب زيد، وما إليك بقاصد عمرو

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basrans say the raised construction is Tamim's dialect and cite a line addressed to Tamim.
rows.anchor: وحكى البصريون أنها لغة تميم، وأنشدوا:

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i locates the raised construction in Tihama and Najd.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي أنها لغة تهامة ونجد.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra' calls the nominative one of two constructions the stronger.
rows.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن الرفع أقوى الوجهين:

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq rejects that preference because Qur'anic and Prophetic Arabic is stronger and more authoritative.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وهذا غلط كتاب الله عز وجل ولغة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقوى وأولى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafsa's codex has the wording with an explicit bāʾ before بشر.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف حفصة رضي الله عنها «ما هذا ببشر»

rows.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر
rows.claim: The women saw Yusuf as more beautiful than humans, indeed as an angel.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: وذكرت النسوة أن صورة يوسف أحسن من صورة البشر

rows.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر
rows.claim: One reading of حاش لله clears Yusuf of the wife's seduction charge; لله means for fear of God, so the comparison concerns moral purity.
rows.anchor: «حاش لله» تبرئة ليوسف عما رمته به امرأة العزيز من المراودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moral-purity reading reconciles their angel comparison with the statement that humans were created in the best form.
rows.anchor: أنه في التبرئة عن المعاصي كالملائكة فعلى هذا لا تناقض.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the women meant Yusuf's extreme beauty made him unlike humans and assumed angels were more beautiful; the cited human-creation verse was not known to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد تنزيهه عن مشابهة البشر في الصورة، لفرط جماله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not obliged to append a correction whenever scripture reports an unbeliever's falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهذا باطل إذ لا وجوب على الله تعالى، وليس كل ما يخبر به الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a beautiful person an angel is ordinary hyperbole for unmatched appearance or purity; people do not see angels.
rows.anchor: أهل العرف قد يقولون في القبيح كأنه شيطان، وفي الحسن كأنه ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet describes Yusuf as too angelic to be human, illustrating the women's comparison.
rows.anchor: تنزل من جو السماء يصوب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan's reading بشرى means Yusuf is no slave for sale; the verbal noun stands for a passive participle, as in sea game for what is caught.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن: «ما هذا بشرى» بكسر الباء والشين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, he cannot be valued at any price; bāʾ belongs to an omitted predicate, as in denying that something costs a thousand.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: ما هذا بثمن، أي مثله لا يثمن ولا يقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading is preferable because the next phrase intensifies the angel comparison and بشرى would be written with final yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة أشبه لأن بعده «إن هذا إلا ملك كريم»

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: When the women were captivated, the wife defended herself: ذلك means this, and what they blamed her for was loving him.
rows.anchor: و«ذلك» بمعنى «هذا» وهو اختيار الطبري.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to love and ذلك keeps its usual sense: that love is what they blamed her for.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الهاء للحب، و«ذلك» على بابه، والمعنى: ذلكن الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawm means describing someone with an ugly or blameworthy quality.
rows.anchor: واللوم الوصف بالقبيح. ثم أقرت وقالت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife admits seducing Yusuf; استعصم means he refrained, and عصمة is named for preventing sin.
rows.anchor: أي امتنع وسميت العصمة عصمة لأنها تمنع من ارتكاب المعصية.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: استعصم may instead be understood as استعصى, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «استعصم» أي استعصى، والمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She renews the seduction in front of the women and threatens prison now that she no longer fears blame, unlike her initial private approach.
rows.anchor: عاودته المراودة بمحضر منهن، وهتكت جلباب الحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The الصاغرين are the humiliated and abased.
rows.anchor: أي الأذلاء. وخط المصحف «وليكونا» بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex writes وليكونا with alif; it is read with a light emphatic nūn, while ليسجنن has the heavy nūn.
rows.anchor: وخط المصحف «وليكونا» بالألف وتقرأ بنون مخففة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light emphatic nūn is written with pausal alif, as in 96:15 and al-A'sha's line.
rows.anchor: ونحوها الوقف عليها بالألف، كقول الأعشى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet intended a form ending in light emphatic nūn; when paused, it is written with alif as فاعبدا.
rows.anchor: فلما وقف عليه كان الوقف بالألف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's knowledge follows from leaving the king's religion and includes dreams, incoming meals, and God's religion.
rows.anchor: العلم بتأويل رؤياكما، والعلم بما يأتيكما من طعامكما والعلم بدين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prioritizes religion and invites the prisoners to Islam before interpreting their dreams.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لم يعبر لهما حتى دعاهما إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: He knew one prisoner would be killed and invited both to Islam so the condemned man could gain salvation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: علم أن أحدهما مقتول فدعاهما إلى الإسلام ليسعدا به.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, he disliked interpreting a dream that foretold harm to one man and redirected them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن يوسف كره أن يعبر لهما ما سألاه لما علمه من المكروه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the food appears in a dream and Yusuf explains it while they are awake; he attributes this knowledge to revelation rather than divination.
rows.anchor: «إلا نبأتكما» بتفسيره في اليقظة، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The king prepared a particular meal for someone he intended to execute, so the promise concerns food arriving while awake.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان الملك إذا أراد قتل إنسان صنع له طعاما معروفا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Yusuf disclosed hidden matters comparably to Jesus.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كان يخبرهما بما غاب، كعيسى عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: His invitation to Islam made foretelling the unseen a sign by which the prisoners could recognize his truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما دعاهما بذلك إلى الإسلام، وجعل المعجزة التي يستدلان بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were true prophets; ما كان means it was improper for them to associate anything with God, and من adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: { ما كان } أي ما ينبغي. { لنآ أن نشرك بالله من شيء } «من» للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor means Yusuf was protected from adultery and believers from shirk; another view means prophethood for the family and messengership for people.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى عصمته من الزنى. { وعلى الناس } أي على المؤمنين الذين عصمهم الله من الشرك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to thank God for monotheism and faith.
rows.anchor: ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون } على نعمة التوحيد والإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two are addressed as prison companions because they have stayed there together a long time, like the companions of Paradise or Fire.
rows.anchor: أي يا ساكني السجن وذكر الصحبة لطول مقامهما فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The separate lords may differ in size, whether small, large, or intermediate, or may differ in number.
rows.anchor: أأرباب متفرقون } أي في الصغر والكبر والتوسط، أو متفرقون في العدد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The address may include both prisoners and other inmates; their idols cannot harm or benefit, unlike the one God who conquers all.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب لهما ولأهل السجن، وكان بين أيديهم أصنام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, multiple gods would have divided wills and some would dominate others, so they would not be gods.
rows.anchor: لو تعدد الإله لتفرقوا في الإرادة ولعلا بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's question echoes the challenge in 27:59 about whether God or the partners people associate are better.
rows.anchor: آلله خير أما يشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols have names but no real divine qualities; alternatively, they are inert objects with only the name of divinity.
rows.anchor: أي من دون الله إلا ذوات أسماء لا معاني لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Yusuf began by addressing two men, he means all who share their idolatry; the omitted second object is that they named them gods.
rows.anchor: وقال: «ما تعبدون» وقد ابتدأ بخطاب الاثنين لأنه قصد جميع من هو على مثل حالهما

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr glosses سلطان as proof.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: { من سلطان } أي من حجة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment belongs to God, creator of all; He commands worship of Him alone, the upright religion, though most people do not know.
rows.anchor: { إن الحكم إلا لله } الذي هو خالق الكل. { أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra' allows the accusative reading أضغاث أحلام.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ويجوز «أضغاث أحلام»

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the accusative remote: the king saw no interpretable thing, only mixed-up dreams.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: النصب بعيد، لأن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ضغث is a mixed bunch of herbs or grasses; a poet compares a confused dream to one.
rows.anchor: وواحد الأضغاث ضغث، يقال لكل مختلط من بقل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: They deny knowledge of dreams that have no interpretation, rather than denying all dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى بتأويل الأحلام المختلطة، نفوا عن أنفسهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they deny skill in dream interpretation generally.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نفوا عن أنفسهم علم التعبير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bundles may contain both true and false visions; the cupbearer's offer shows the counselors could not interpret, not that no interpretation existed.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال الساقي: «أنا أنبئكم بتأويله» فعلم أن القوم عجزوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the counselors only wanted to erase the dream from the king's mind, implying they did have interpretive knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم لم يقصدوا تفسيرا، وإنما أرادوا محوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the claim that a dream necessarily takes effect at its first interpretation: Yusuf's forecast came true, unlike their dismissal.
rows.anchor: دليل على بطلان قول من يقول: إن الرؤيا على أول ما تعبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also refutes the claim that a dream hangs on a bird until interpreted and then occurs.
rows.anchor: وفيها دليل على فساد أن الرؤيا على رجل طائر، فإذا عبرت وقعت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحلام is plural of حلم, what a sleeper sees; the word is connected with sleep's patient, quiet state.
rows.anchor: و«الأحلام» جمع حلم، والحلم بالضم مايراه النائم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some assign this statement to the wife, continuing her confession that she did not lie about Yusuf or speak against him while he was absent.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هو من قول امرأة العزيز، وهو متصل بقولها:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On this reading, she admits her wrongdoing and recognizes that her Lord forgives and shows mercy.
rows.anchor: بل أنا راودته وعلى هذا هي كانت مقرة بالصانع، ولهذا قالت

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others attribute the words to Yusuf: by returning the messenger, he wanted the Aziz to know he had not betrayed him in his absence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول يوسف أي قال يوسف: ذلك الأمر الذي فعلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf uses the third person ليعلم while speaking before the king out of deference to him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال يوسف ذلك بحضرة الملك، وقال: «ليعلم» على الغائب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Gabriel challenged Yusuf in prison about loosening his garment and sitting as a man does with a woman; Yusuf then disclaimed purity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: جاء الرسول إلى يوسف عليه السلام بالخبر وجبريل معه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the wife challenged Yusuf about loosening his trousers, and he answered that he did not acquit himself.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إنما قالت له امرأة العزيز ولا حين حللت سراويلك يا يوسف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the Aziz say he had not betrayed Yusuf in his absence and had not neglected to reward his trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «ذلك ليعلم» من قول العزيز أي ذلك ليعلم يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah does not guide traitors through their schemes.
rows.anchor: معناه أن الله لا يهدي الخائنين بكيدهم.

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says the apparent reading assigns both ذلك ليعلم and وما أبرئ نفسي to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري: فالظاهر أن قوله: «ذلك ليعلم» وقوله: «وما أبرىء نفسي»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the words may belong to the wife, that reading is preferable because it clears Yusuf of loosening his garments; if he said them, the thought crossed his mind as discussed under 12:24.
rows.anchor: إذا احتمل أن يكون من قول المرأة فالقول به أولى حتى نبرىء يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Anbari reports that some treat the wife's speech from her confession through إن ربي غفور رحيم as one continuous passage; Qurtubi says he does not choose that view.
rows.anchor: ولسنا نختار هذا القول ولا نذهب إليه.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Yusuf feared praising himself because self-purification is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: لما قال يوسف: «ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an forbids self-purification and Qurtubi says the matter was explained in Surat al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم [النجم: 32] وقد بيناه في «النساء».

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some make the Aziz the speaker, disclaiming ill suspicion of Yusuf.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول العزيز أي وما أبرىء نفسي من سوء الظن بيوسف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is strongly inclined to evil, meaning that it desires evil.
rows.anchor: { إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء } أي مشتهية له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected because it excludes the person shown mercy and protected from the soul that commands evil.
rows.anchor: وهو استثناء منقطع، لأنه استثناء المرحوم بالعصمة من النفس الأمارة بالسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an often uses ما in the sense of من, as in the instruction about marrying what is lawful of women.
rows.anchor: و«ما» بمعنى من كثير قال الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic parable calls the soul a bad companion: indulging it leads to a bad end, while disciplining it leads to a good end.
rows.anchor: «فوالذي نفسي بيده إنها لنفوسكم التي بين جنوبكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After verifying Yusuf's innocence and honesty and seeing his patience and good character, the king elevated him and asked that he be brought as a confidant.
rows.anchor: لما ثبت للملك براءته مما نسب إليه وتحقق في القصة أمانته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king first merely asked that Yusuf be brought, then after Yusuf's further conduct asked to make him his chosen confidant.
rows.anchor: فانظر إلى قول الملك أولا حين تحقق علمه «ائتوني به» فقط

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Yusuf paused at the door, invoked God's sufficiency and majesty, then entered.
rows.anchor: وروي عن وهب بن منبه قال: لما دعي يوسف وقف بالباب

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says the king descended, prostrated to Yusuf, seated him beside himself, and declared him powerful and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: ثم دخل فلما نظر إليه الملك نزل عن سريره فخر له ساجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf says he can guard the treasuries and manage them; another explanation makes him skilled in accounting or languages.
rows.anchor: «عليم» بوجوه تصرفاتها. وقيل: حافظ للحساب، عليم بالألسن.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God have mercy on Yusuf: without his request to oversee the treasuries, the king would have appointed him at once rather than after a year.
rows.anchor: يرحم الله أخي يوسف لو لم يقل اجعلني على خزائن الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Yusuf's appointment was delayed a year because he did not say إن شاء الله.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما تأخر تمليكه إلى سنة لأنه لم يقل إن شاء الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Yusuf greeted the king in Arabic and Hebrew as the languages of Ishmael and of his forefathers; the king knew seventy languages and Yusuf answered in each.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يتكلم بسبعين لسانا، فكلما تكلم الملك بلسان أجابه يوسف بذلك اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative places Yusuf at thirty when the king seated him and asked him to recount the dream.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف إذ ذاك ابن ثلاثين سنة ثم أجلسه على سريره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf recounts seven fat, beautiful cows from the Nile, then seven gaunt cows that devour them without gaining weight.
rows.anchor: رأيت سبع بقرات سمان شهبا غرا حسانا، كشف لك عنهن النيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also recounts seven full green ears destroyed by wind and leaves from seven dry ears, all growing in one place.
rows.anchor: إذا بسبع سنابل خضر طريات ناعمات ممتلئات حبا وماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf advises collecting food during fertile years, storing grain in its stalks, feeding stalks to animals and grain to people, and distributing it during famine.
rows.anchor: أرى أن تجمع الطعام، وتزرع زرعا كثيرا في هذه السنين المخصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خزائن is plural of خزانة, and its definite article substitutes for an omitted possessive construction.
rows.anchor: وهي جمع خزانة ودخلت الألف واللام عوضا من الإضافة

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's couplet is cited as evidence for the preceding grammatical construction involving the article.
rows.anchor: لهم شيمة لم يعطها الله غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أستخلصه is jussive as the response to the king's command; this points to Yusuf's non-betrayal statement being made in prison, though it may have been said before the king and repeated later.
rows.anchor: جزم لأنه جواب الأمر وهذا يدل على أن قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the king hears Yusuf's dream interpretation, مكين means empowered with effective speech, and أمين means one from whom betrayal is not feared.
rows.anchor: أي متمكن نافذ القول، «أمين» لا تخاف غدرا.

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik calls Egypt the treasury of the earth and reads خزائن الأرض as guarding it, with an understood genitive.
rows.anchor: سمعت مالك بن أنس يقول: مصر خزانة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafiz means reliable in what he was entrusted with and alim means knowledgeable about its affairs.
rows.anchor: { إني حفيظ } لما وليت { عليم } بأمره.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An exegetical gloss says Yusuf was an accountant and scribe, the first to write on paper.
rows.anchor: وفي التفسير: إني حاسب كاتب وأنه أول من كتب في القراطيس.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss makes hafiz someone who calculates provisions and alim someone who knows the famine years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «حفيظ» لتقدير الأقوات «عليم» بسني المجاعات.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the prophetic report that Yusuf's request delayed his appointment for a year; without it the king would appoint him at once.
rows.anchor: رحم الله أخي يوسف لو لم يقل اجعلني على خزائن الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the king crowned and invested Yusuf after the year, seated him on an ornate throne, and delegated Egypt to him in place of Qiftir.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما انصرمت السنة من يوم سأل الإمارة دعاه الملك فتوجه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh gave Yusuf all his authority, Qiftir died, and the king married Yusuf to Ra'il, who bore two sons.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان لفرعون ملك مصر خزائن كثيرة غير الطعام

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb places Yusuf's marriage to Zulaikha between the brothers' visits; she became poor and blind from weeping and encountered Yusuf in his procession.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: إنما كان تزويجه زليخاء امرأة العزيز بين دخلتي الإخوة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: In Wahb's account, Zulaikha confesses her past ignorance and love; Yusuf offers marriage if she is widowed or support if married, and she says she still longs for his face.
rows.anchor: أنا التي كنت أخدمك على صدور قدمي، وأرجل جمتك بيدي

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: The account says Yusuf prayed for her youth, beauty, and sight to return; she became a virgin bride and bore two sons, as a reward for Yusuf's chastity.
rows.anchor: فسأل الله تعالى أن يعيد إليها شبابها وجمالها وبصرها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some scholars allow a virtuous person to serve an immoral or unbelieving ruler if given a sphere to reform lawfully; serving the ruler's sinful whims is forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل العلم: في هذه الآية ما يبيح للرجل الفاضل أن يعمل للرجل الفاجر

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say this appointment was unique to Yusuf and is impermissible today; Qurtubi prefers conditional permission.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إن هذا كان ليوسف خاصة، وهذا اليوم غير جائز والأول أولى

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi presents permission when an appointee administers justice, since Yusuf served Pharaoh, and prohibition because appointment aids and legitimizes oppressors.
rows.anchor: فقد اختلف الناس في جواز الولاية من قبله على قولين

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Replies say Yusuf's Pharaoh was righteous unlike Moses' tyrant, or that Yusuf oversaw property rather than the ruler's acts.
rows.anchor: أن فرعون يوسف كان صالحا، وإنما الطاغي فرعون موسى.

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi distinguishes fixed charitable dues, which may be administered; discretionary public funds, which may not; and adjudication, allowed by consent but not by coercion.
rows.anchor: والأصح من إطلاق هذين القولين أن يفصل ما يتولاه من جهة الظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God placed far more love for her in Yusuf's heart; he asked why she no longer loved him, and she answered that God's love now occupied her above all else.
rows.anchor: وفيما روي أن الله تعالى ألقى في قلب يوسف من محبتها أضعاف ما كان في قلبها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura not to seek office: requested appointment leaves the holder unaided, while appointment without asking brings aid.
rows.anchor: يا عبد الرحمن لا تسأل الإمارة فإنك إن أعطيتها عن مسألة وكلت إليها

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa says two companions asked for office; the Prophet said they would not appoint someone who sought it.
rows.anchor: لن أو لا نستعمل على عملنا من أراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf sought office because he alone could ensure justice, reform, and poor people's rights; if no qualified replacement exists, a judge or market inspector may have a duty to seek appointment and state his qualifications.
rows.anchor: أن يوسف عليه السلام إنما طلب الولاية لأنه علم أنه لا أحد يقوم مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If another qualified person can fill the role, it is better not to seek it; eagerness despite its hazards suggests self-interest and risks being left to one's own weakness.
rows.anchor: فالأولى ألا يطلب لقوله عليه السلام لعبد الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith means one who refuses office out of fear of its hazards may receive divine help if it is later imposed on him.
rows.anchor: ومن أباها لعلمه بآفاتها، ولخوفه من التقصير في حقوقها فر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf cited relevant custody and knowledge, not noble lineage or physical beauty.
rows.anchor: ولا قال: إني جميل مليح، إنما قال: «إني حفيظ عليم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He introduced his qualities to people who did not know him, and saw the office as an urgent duty because no one else could perform it; that is the strongest explanation.
rows.anchor: إنما قال ذلك عند من لا يعرفه فأراد تعريف نفسه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: A person may state relevant knowledge or merit, but self-praise without a task connection or outward evidence is forbidden; Yusuf's necessity and hoped-for benefit excused him.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا على الإطلاق في عموم الصفات، ولكنه مخصوص فيما اقترن بوصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's enabling Yusuf in the land parallels drawing him close to the king and rescuing him from prison: God empowered him to do as he wished.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا الإنعام الذي أنعمنا عليه في تقريبه إلى قلب الملك، وإنجائه من السجن

rows.speaker: الكيا الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari sees evidence that stratagems may reach lawful good, public benefit, or recovery of rights; Qurtubi rejects this inference here.
rows.anchor: دليل على إجازة الحيلة في التوصل إلى المباح، وما فيه الغبطة والصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says al-Kiya's inference is rejected and will be addressed later.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا مردود على ما يأتي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb occurs as مكناه and مكنا له; another Qur'anic passage has مكناهم.
rows.anchor: يقال: مكناه ومكنا له، قال الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the senior king al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan appointed Yusuf to Itfir's office and dismissed Itfir.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: استخلف الملك الأكبر الوليد بن الريان يوسف على عمل إطفير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the king became Muslim through Yusuf.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: وأسلم على يديه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Yusuf became king after a year and a half.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ملكه بعد سنة ونصف.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that if Yusuf had added إن شاء الله to his claim of competence, he would have ruled immediately.
rows.anchor: لو أن يوسف قال إني حفيظ عليم إن شاء الله لملك في وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts differ over Zulaikha: one says Yusuf married Itfir's widow and had two sons; another says he did not marry her but kept her in his household until death, which Mavardi says conflicts with Wahb.
rows.anchor: ومن زعم أنها زليخاء قال: لم يتزوجها يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf invited Egyptians to Islam, governed justly, and became beloved; reports by Wahb, al-Suddi, and Ibn Abbas say he stored each fertile year's grain through seven abundant years.
rows.anchor: ولما فوض الملك أمر مصر إلى يوسف تلطف بالناس، وجعل يدعوهم إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wisdom saying names unusual hunger and appetite plus severe food scarcity as famine's two signs; both appeared in Yusuf's time and the king was relieved after Yusuf prayed.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الحكمة: للجوع والقحط علامتان: إحداهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the king woke hungry as famine began and Yusuf identified the crisis; the first year's reserves were exhausted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما كان ابتداء القحط بينا الملك في جوف الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Yusuf sold food successively for money, jewelry, livestock, servants, land, families, and finally the Egyptians' own persons during the seven famine years.
rows.anchor: فباعهم أول سنة بالنقود، حتى لم يبق بمصر دينار ولا درهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When the king gave him authority, Yusuf freed all Egyptians, restored their property and the king's rule, and said he had not saved them from hunger to enslave them.
rows.anchor: إني لم أعتقهم من الجوع لأستعبدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf ate sparingly so he would remember the hungry; he made the king eat at midday so he would taste hunger and remember the poor.
rows.anchor: إني أخاف إن شبعت أن أنسى الجائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy means God's beneficence, and not wasting the doers of good means preserving their reward.
rows.anchor: أي بإحساننا والرحمة النعمة والإحسان. { ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب
rows.claim: They identify the rewarded people as patient through the well, enslavement, prison, and restraint from the wife's advances.
rows.anchor: يعني الصابرين لصبره في الجب، وفي الرق، وفي السجن

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi gives two accounts of Yusuf's position: reward for his trials, or a divine gift with his afterlife reward still intact.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه ثواب من الله تعالى على ما ابتلاه. الثاني: أنه أنعم الله عليه بذلك تفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife reward is better and greater because it endures, unlike the world's temporary reward; the verse applies generally to believers who fear God.
rows.anchor: لأن أجر الآخرة دائم، وأجر الدنيا ينقطع وظاهر الآية العموم في كل مؤمن متق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The poems console the wrongfully imprisoned by presenting Yusuf as a model: patience leads from confinement and distress to kingship, safety, and relief.
rows.anchor: أقام جميل الصبر في الحبس برهة فآل به الصبر الجميل إلى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's omission of the brothers' journey to Egypt is an example of concise eloquence.
rows.anchor: وهذا من اختصار القرآن المعجز.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: When famine reached Canaan, Jacob sent his sons for provisions; Yusuf's gentleness, mercy, justice, and conduct were famous, and he personally gave each person a wasq of food.
rows.anchor: بعث يعقوب عليه السلام ولده للميرة، وذاع أمر يوسف عليه السلام في الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers did not recognize Yusuf because they had left him as a child and could not imagine a former slave ruling after forty years.
rows.anchor: لأنهم خلفوه صبيا، ولم يتوهموا أنه بعد العبودية يبلغ إلى تلك الحال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They may have failed to recognize him because they assumed he was an unbelieving king, or because his silk, gold collar, and crown looked unlike their familiar clothing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أنكروه لأنهم اعتقدوا أنه ملك كافر: وقيل: رأوه لابس حرير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations are that they saw him behind a curtain or God miraculously prevented recognition to test Jacob.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم رأوه وراء ستر فلم يعرفوه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جهز means equipping travelers; a bridal جهاز is a trousseau, and here it means the food they bought. Some Kufans allow الجهاز with a kasra on jīm.
rows.anchor: يقال جهزت القوم تجهيزا أي تكلفت لهم بجهازهم للسفر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says ten brothers had eleven camels and told Yusuf their youngest stayed with their father; Yusuf asked why and wanted to verify the story and see the beloved brother.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: وكان مع إخوة يوسف أحد عشر بعيرا، وهم عشرة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: One report says the brothers left Shimon as hostage until they returned with Benjamin.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنهم تركوا عنده شمعون رهينة، حتى يأتوا بأخيه بنيامين.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a dialogue through an interpreter: Yusuf suspected spies because of their different language and dress; they said one brother died and another stayed with their father.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس قال يوسف للترجمان قل لهم: لغتكم مخالفة للغتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf demands the younger brother so he can see him and test whether the brothers are truthful.
rows.anchor: فأنا أرضى بذلك { ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he gives full measure and adds a camel-load for their brother; full measure may mean a favorable price or an ample, accurate measure.
rows.anchor: ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل } أي أتمه ولا أبخسه، وأزيدكم حمل بعير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes خير المنزلين to mean the most generous host; another sense is a trusted place to stay, from منزل as a dwelling rather than food.
rows.anchor: أنه خير المضيفين، لأنه أحسن ضيافتهم قاله مجاهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He threatens no more grain without Benjamin; ولا تقربون means he will not treat them as close guests, indirectly urging them to return, not banning their return.
rows.anchor: أي لا أنزلكم عندي منزلة القريب، ولم يرد أنهم يبعدون منه ولا يعودون إليه

rows.speaker: السدي والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Shimon was kept hostage; al-Kalbi says he was chosen because he had spoken best and advised best on the day Yusuf was thrown in the well.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: إنما اختار شمعون منهم لأنه كان يوم الجب أجملهم قولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تقربون is jussive as a prohibition, so its nūn and yāʾ are omitted.
rows.anchor: و«تقربون» في موضع جزم بالنهي، فلذلك حذفت منه النون وحذفت الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to ask their father for Benjamin and guarantee and contrive to bring him.
rows.anchor: { وإنا لفاعلون } أي لضامنون المجيء به، ومحتالون في ذلك.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: To explain Yusuf's demand despite grief to Jacob, one view says God commanded it as a test to increase Jacob's reward; others say Yusuf wanted to alert Jacob, intensify the reunion's joy, or spend time first with Benjamin.
rows.anchor: عن هذا أربعة أجوبة: أحدها: يجوز أن يكون الله عز وجل أمره بذلك ابتلاء ليعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that God ordered the test is the strongest of the four answers.
rows.anchor: والأول أظهر، والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: They read لفتيته; Abu Hatim and al-Nahhas also prefer this form.
rows.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة وأبي عمرو وعاصم وهي اختيار أبي حاتم والنحاس

rows.speaker: سائر الكوفيين
rows.claim: Other Kufans read لفتيانه; Abu Ubayd prefers it and says the Ibn Masud codex has it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سائر الكوفيين «لفتيانه» وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi says both forms are good Arabic, like the two forms for boys.
rows.anchor: قال الثعلبي: وهما لغتان جيدتان مثل الصبيان والصبية

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas objects that فتيان conflicts with the received consonantal text and relies on a disconnected report; فتية better fits a small number of helpers.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: «لفتيانه» مخالف للسواد الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendants arranged provisions and could place the brothers' payment in their bags; they may have been free helpers.
rows.anchor: وكان هؤلاء الفتية يسوون جهازهم، ولهذا أمكنهم جعل بضاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their payment was the cost of the food, perhaps dirhams or dinars; Ibn Abbas instead says it was travelers' goods such as shoes and leather.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت دراهم ودنانير. وقال ابن عباس: النعال والأدم ومتاع المسافر

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says رَحل can mean either a container or a house.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: يقال للوعاء رحل، وللبيت رحل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning the payment could help travel back, prompt a return because they would not accept unpaid food, avoid charging his father and brothers, or display favor and attract them.
rows.anchor: قيل: ليستعينوا بذلك على الرجوع لشراء الطعام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers explain Yusuf refused further grain without Benjamin and that Shimon remains hostage until they establish their story.
rows.anchor: لأنه قال لهم: «فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original نكتال loses its alif in the jussive because of the meeting of two still consonants.
rows.anchor: والأصل نكتال فحذفت الضمة من اللام للجزم، وحذفت الألف

rows.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: They read نكتل with nūn, preferred by Abu Ubayd because all brothers participate in measuring.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أهل الحرمين وأبي عمرو وعاصم «نكتل» بالنون

rows.speaker: سائر الكوفيين
rows.claim: They read يكتل with yāʾ; al-Nahhas says this need not mean Benjamin alone, because the wording can imply he joins them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سائر الكوفيين «يكتل» بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asks whether he can trust them after their earlier failure with Yusuf, then says God's protection is better than theirs.
rows.anchor: أي قد فرطتم في يوسف فكيف آمنكم على أخيه!.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings حفظا and حافظا are respectively an accusative clarifier and a circumstantial adjective; both mean God's safeguarding is better.
rows.anchor: فالله خير حفظا } نصب على البيان، وهذه قراءة أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b says God swore to return both sons after Jacob called Him the best guardian and relied on Him.
rows.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: لما قال يعقوب: «فالله خير حافظا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما نبغي can ask what more they need after full measure and returned payment, reassuring their father; alternatively, they say they want no money or goods beyond the returned payment.
rows.anchor: «ما» استفهام في موضع نصب والمعنى: أي شيء نطلب وراء هذا؟

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: Alqama reads رِدَّت with kasra on rāʾ, explained by the original doubled form and vowel transfer under assimilation.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علقمة «ردت إلينا» بكسر الراء لأن الأصل رددت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نَمير means bringing food to the family; the cited poem uses مائرا for a provisions-gatherer.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { ونمير أهلنا } أي نجلب لهم الطعام قال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poem uses مائرا for someone sent to procure provisions, witnessing the meaning of نَمير.
rows.anchor: بعثتك مائرا فمكثت حولا

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads نُمير with damma on nūn, meaning they will assist their family with provisions.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي بضم النون، أي نعينهم على الميرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra measure is one camel-load for Benjamin.
rows.anchor: { ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير } أي حمل بعير لبنيامين.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Mawthiq is a binding pledge; al-Suddi says the brothers swore to return Benjamin and not surrender him.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: حلفوا بالله ليردنه إليه ولا يسلمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لتأتنني marks an oath; Mujahid says surrounded means killed or dead, Qatada says overcome, and al-Zajjaj notes the phrase is accusative.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لتأتنني } لام القسم. { إلا أن يحاط بكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is keeper of the oath or guardian of the covenant and just manager of affairs.
rows.anchor: أي حافظ للحلف. وقيل: حفيظ للعهد قائم بالتدبير والعدل.

rows.speaker: مالك وجميع أصحابه وأكثر العلماء
rows.claim: They allow personal surety for financial obligations; al-Shafi'i weakens it but also has an opinion like Malik, while Uthman al-Batti assigns compensation for failed surety in retaliation or wounds.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك وجميع أصحابه وأكثر العلماء: هي جائزة إذا كان المتحمل به مالا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers Malik's distinction: surety may secure money, but not a criminal penalty or discretionary punishment.
rows.anchor: والصواب تفرقة مالك في ذلك، وأنها تكون في المال، ولا تكون في حد أو تعزير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وقتادة وغيرهم
rows.claim: Jacob feared the evil eye because his eleven handsome and strong sons traveled together, so he told them to enter Egypt by separate gates; Egypt had four gates.
rows.anchor: خشي عليهم العين فأمرهم ألا يدخلوا مصر من باب واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports guarding against the real evil eye; a prophetic report says it can put a man in the grave and a camel in the pot.
rows.anchor: فيكون فيها دليل على التحرز من العين، والعين حق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet seeks refuge in God's complete words from Satan, harmful creatures, and every malignant eye.
rows.anchor: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامة من كل شيطان وهامة ومن كل عين لامة

rows.speaker: مالك عن محمد بن أبي أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف
rows.claim: Amir ibn Rabi'a admired Sahl ibn Hunayf's fair skin and Sahl became ill; the Prophet said the eye is real, told Amir to invoke blessing and wash, and Sahl recovered after the water was poured on him.
rows.anchor: علام يقتل أحدكم أخاه ألا بركت إن العين حق توضأ له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says a woman's admiring comment about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was followed by his collapse and that she washed for him.
rows.anchor: وركب سعد بن أبي وقاص يوما فنظرت إليه امرأة فقالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports support scholarly consensus and Sunni teaching that the evil eye can harm or kill; innovators deny it, but prophetic teaching and experience refute them, and it acts only by God's will.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول علماء الأمة، ومذهب أهل السنة وقد أنكرته طوائف من المبتدعة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i recounts an evil-eyed man admiring a cow's milk and causing both the pointed-out and decoy cows to die; the man said admiration brings heat from his eye.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: رأيت رجلا عيونا سمع بقرة تحلب فأعجبه شخبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Muslim who admires something should invoke blessing, which averts harm; the Prophet's rebuke shows the eye harms when blessing is omitted.
rows.anchor: واجب على كل مسلم أعجبه شيء أن يبرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing formula is تبارك الله أحسن الخالقين or اللهم بارك فيه.
rows.anchor: والتبريك أن يقول: تبارك الله أحسن الخالقين! اللهم بارك فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A known person who causes the eye should be ordered to wash and compelled if he refuses, since this may save the afflicted person's life.
rows.anchor: العائن إذا أصاب بعينه ولم يبرك فإنه يؤمر بالاغتسال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some scholars would confine or exile a person known for the evil eye and provide support if poor; Qurtubi notes the Prophet neither confined nor exiled Amir, and a righteous person may cause the eye without sin.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إنه ينفى وحديث مالك الذي ذكرناه يرد هذه الأقوال

rows.speaker: مالك عن حميد بن قيس المكي
rows.claim: A disconnected report says the Prophet saw Ja'far's thin children, heard their caretaker feared the evil eye, and ordered ruqya, saying if anything could precede destiny it would be the eye.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: استرقوا لهما فإنه لو سبق شيء القدر سبقته العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about Ja'far's sons is disconnected, but sound connected routes preserve it from Asma bint Umays; ruqya repels harm and the evil eye weakens people by God's decree, with children said to be more vulnerable.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث منقطع، ولكنه محفوظ لأسماء بنت عميس الخثعمية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the culprit is known, he is ordered to wash as in the Sahl report; if unknown, one seeks ruqya.
rows.anchor: إنما يسترقي من العين إذا لم يعرف العائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob means precautions cannot avert God's decree; judgment and events belong to God, on whom he relies and whom believers should trust.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينفع الحذر مع القدر. { إن الحكم } أي الأمر والقضاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They entered by separate gates; this could not avert harm God intended, and the disconnected exception means Jacob fulfilled a concern by giving this instruction.
rows.anchor: { إلا حاجة } استثناء ليس من الأول. { في نفس يعقوب قضاها }

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Jacob feared the evil eye; later commentators instead say the king might envy or suspect the brothers' strength and number, a view al-Nahhas prefers.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: خشية العين، وقد تقدم القول فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches Muslims to warn a brother of danger and guide him toward safety, since religion is sincere counsel and believers are brothers.
rows.anchor: ودلت هذه الآية على أن المسلم يجب عليه أن يحذر أخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob has religious knowledge from God; alternatively علم means action because knowledge is its first cause.
rows.anchor: { لذو علم لما علمناه } أي بأمر دينه.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yusuf embraced Benjamin and lodged him with himself.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ضمه إليه، وأنزله معه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Yusuf assigned pairs to rooms; Benjamin was alone, so Yusuf took him in and said he feared loneliness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمر أن ينزل كل اثنين في منزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf privately identifies himself as Benjamin's brother and tells him not to grieve over their brothers' behavior.
rows.anchor: وقال له سرا من إخوته: { إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس } أي لا تحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Benjamin recognizes Yusuf, he asks not to be returned; Yusuf says Jacob would grieve more, but Benjamin insists, and Yusuf hides the cup himself unseen or has an associate do it.
rows.anchor: فأبى بنيامين الخروج فقال يوسف: لا يمكن حبسك إلا بعد أن أنسبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تجهيز means sending off or completing an affair; when used of a wounded person, it can mean killing him or finishing him off.
rows.anchor: والتجهيز التسريح وتنجيز الأمر ومنه جهز على الجريح أي قتله

rows.speaker: النقاش عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The siqaya and suwa are the same two-ended vessel with a handle: the king drank from one end and food was measured with the other; anything used for drinking can be called a suwa.
rows.anchor: والسقاية والصواع شيء واحد إناء له رأسان في وسطه مقبض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the king's cup was silver, like a small measure, jeweled and worn on the head; he also defines الصواع as a vessel.
rows.anchor: قال: كان صواع الملك شيء من فضة يشبه المكوك، من فضة مرصع بالجوهر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the cup was made of silver.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كان من فضة.

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says it was gold and measured food as an added honor; another view says scarcity explains its use as a measure.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: كان من ذهب وبه كال طعامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صاع is feminine or masculine: its plural is أصوع in feminine usage and أصواع in masculine usage.
rows.anchor: والصاع يذكر ويؤنث فمن أنثه قال: أصوع مثل أدور

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو صالح
rows.claim: They identify the vessel as a طَرْجَهالة, a Himyari word.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو صالح: الصاع الطرجهالة بلغة حمير.

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Readings include the common صواع, Yahya ibn Ya'mar's صوغ with ghayn, Abu Raja's صوع, Abu's صوع with ṣad damma, Sa'id ibn Jubayr's صياع, and Abu Hurayra's صاع.
rows.anchor: وفيه قراءات: «صواع» قراءة العامة و «صوغ» بالغين المعجمة، وهي قراءة يحيى بن يعمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The herald's أذن is intensive, as if he called repeatedly; العير can mean transport animals or their owners by metonymy.
rows.anchor: «وأذن» للتكثير فكأنه نادى مرارا «أيتها العير».

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says their caravan consisted of donkeys; Abu Ubayda says العير means loaded camels, hence their owners.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان عيرهم حميرا. قال أبو عبيدة: العير الإبل المرحولة المركوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers can be called thieves because they took Yusuf from his father, cast him in the well, and sold him; alternatively, they possess something without the king's consent or knowledge.
rows.anchor: أن القوم كانوا قد سرقوه من أبيه فألقوه في الجب، ثم باعوه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The accusation may be a contrivance to unite Yusuf and Benjamin, assuming Benjamin did not know about the hidden cup; it may also be interrogative to avoid accusing Yusuf of lying.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى الكلام الاستفهام أي أو إنكم لسارقون؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative reading is compared with 26:22, meaning is that a favor you remind me of, so Yusuf is not accused of lying.
rows.anchor: أي أو تلك نعمة تمنها علي؟ والغرض ألا يعزى إلى يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم الكذب.
